name: qa6 store: UX: a comment in the binder note’s properties survives a move
why: A documented limitation (docs/dev/file-format.md): a property write goes through Obsidian’s serializer, which rewrites the whole block and drops comments. Obsidian’s own Properties view does the same.

name: qa6 store: UX: longform: a comment in the index note’s properties survives a reorder
why: The same documented limitation: Obsidian’s serializer drops comments in the properties block.

name: BUG: qa6 writing: setting a status in a note whose properties are hand written (comments, flow lists, quotes, block text, dates, CRLF) changes only the status line
why: The same documented limitation: Obsidian’s serializer rewrites the whole properties block (comments dropped, flow lists and quoting normalised). The note’s text is untouched.

name: BUG: qa9 roundtrip: 4a markdown: headings come back as headings
why: Open (2026-10-09): export writes a heading as large bold text; the only form the importer takes for a heading is Scrivener’s style markers, which other RTF readers show as words. Needs a heading as real Scrivener writes it.

name: qa10 paragraphs typing: BUG: qa10 paragraphs typing: a note of 2,000 tab paragraphs: after jumping to the end, to the middle and scrolling fast no frame draws a tab line as code; typing at the end and in the middle stays marked
why: Open (2026-10-09): about 15 ms after the first key typed at the end of the note, the editor's lines are for a moment unmarked in the page's structure, though no drawn frame shows it (the frame checks pass). Only in this test's full sequence; cause not found.

name: qa10 paragraphs: NIT: restarting (the plugin disabled and enabled) with a tab-paragraph note open in the editor and in reading view: from the enabling on, no frame draws a tab paragraph with a guide line or without its indent
why: Left on purpose (2026-10-09): for about three frames as the plugin loads, the editor has its reading before Obsidian has added the stylesheet. Holding the reading back would show those frames as code instead.
